question: Supplier S-103 will miss its next RM-103 shipment by four weeks. Handle it.
answer:
I've ordered 3,300 units of RM-103 (Glycerin USP) from the backup supplier S-111 for plant PL-01. Two gaps still need other teams: S-111 isn't approved to ship to PL-02, and nobody can yet say whether the late shipment will cause a shortage of finished product.

**The delay and what it affects**
- **Late shipment:** S-103's next RM-103 shipment is PO000210, 3,300 units, promised for 2026-10-03. Four weeks late puts it around 2026-10-31. S-103 has three more open RM-103 orders due 10-10, 10-18 and 10-25, which may slip too.
- **Products affected:** at PL-01, RM-103 goes into Lacrivia 5 mL and 10 mL and Cyclosporine 0.05% 5 mL. At PL-02, it goes into Oculon 2.5 mL and 5 mL through an ingredient we buy from suppliers S-202/S-203 (CMP-320). I used the current bill of materials, not the old legacy copy, which hasn't been updated since 2024-11-30.
- **Backup supplier:** S-111 is active and approved for RM-103 at PL-01 only. S-103 is approved for both PL-01 and PL-02.
- **Stock at the distribution centres (2026-09-25):** the East centre (DC-EAST) is nearly out of Lacrivia. It has 46 units of the 5 mL against a safety stock of 471 and about 237/week of demand, and 34 units of the 10 mL against 233 and about 110/week. This started on 2026-08-21, while S-103 was still shipping on time, so it wasn't caused by this delay, but the delay makes it worse. Every other product is above safety stock at every centre.

**What I did**
1. **Purchase requisition PR-BA7384C1:** 3,300 units of RM-103 from S-111, shipped to PL-01, needed by 2026-10-23. That date allows for S-111's usual lead time of about 23 days, with a request to expedite. It's on top of S-111's open order PO000228 (5,300 units, due 10-17).
2. **Case CASE-518E77A4 (Procurement / Supplier Quality):**
   - Update PO000210's date in the order system and confirm with S-103 whether the next three orders are also late.
   - Deal with the PL-02 gap: either get S-111 approved for PL-02 quickly or confirm PL-02 has enough RM-103.
   - Check whether S-202/S-203 depend on S-103's glycerin.
   - Have both plants confirm their RM-103 cover through 10-31.
3. **Case CASE-0CFFD66C (Supply Planning Lead):** sets out the East Lacrivia problem and an option to move stock in from the Central and West centres. That would mean about 276 + 278 units of the 5 mL and 120 + 135 units of the 10 mL, and it would take those centres below their own safety stock. The case also suggests splitting East's supply between its two wholesalers, W-01 and W-02, by their shipment history if moving stock isn't enough.

**What I did not do, and why**
- **No order from S-111 to PL-02**, because S-111 isn't approved to ship there.
- **No stock-transfer or allocation approval request, and no allocation.** The approval form needs a dollar amount, and neither database has unit cost or price data. I left the decision to the Supply Planning Lead rather than enter a made-up value.
- **No messages to wholesalers or account teams.** No finished-product shortage caused by this delay is confirmed yet, and the wholesaler inventory feed returned an error (data not yet loaded), so I couldn't check how much stock they hold.
- **No change to PO000210 itself.** I don't have a tool to edit purchase orders, so that's in the Procurement case.
- **No commercial data used.** Demand figures come from shipment history only. I used the commercial database just to match product codes.

**Assumptions**
- "Next shipment" means PO000210, and replacing its full 3,300 units is the right amount. I couldn't work out how long the plants' current RM-103 will last because the data has no plant inventory.
- Weekly demand is the average shipped to wholesalers over the last 13 weeks.

 SELECT b.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID, b.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID, b.QTY_PER, b.EFF_FROM, b.EFF_TO, 1 lvl FROM dbo.BOM b WHERE b.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID='RM-103'

SELECT b1.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID c0, b1.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID p1, b1.QTY_PER q1, b1.EFF_FROM f1, b1.EFF_TO t1,
 b2.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID p2, b2.QTY_PER q2, b2.EFF_TO t2,
 b3.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID p3, b3.QTY_PER q3, b3.EFF_TO t3,
 b4.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID p4, b4.EFF_TO t4
FROM dbo.BOM b1
LEFT JOIN dbo.BOM b2 ON b2.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID=b1.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID
LEFT JOIN dbo.BOM b3 ON b3.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID=b2.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID
LEFT JOIN dbo.BOM b4 ON b4.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID=b3.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID
WHERE b1.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID='RM-103'

SELECT b.*, 'parent_of_fg' k FROM dbo.BOM b WHERE CHILD_MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-2001','FG-2002','FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003')
UNION ALL
SELECT b.*, 'path' FROM dbo.BOM b WHERE CHILD_MATERIAL_ID IN ('CMP-320','SEMI-060','FILL-2001','FILL-2002','SEMI-044','SEMI-045','FILL-1001','FILL-1002','FILL-1003')

SELECT m.MATERIAL_ID, m.MATERIAL_DESC, m.MATERIAL_TYP, m.PACK_SZ, x.NDC, pm.PLANT_ID FROM dbo.MATERIAL m LEFT JOIN dbo.MATERIAL_NDC_XREF x ON x.MATERIAL_ID=m.MATERIAL_ID LEFT JOIN dbo.PLANT_MATERIAL pm ON pm.MATERIAL_ID=m.MATERIAL_ID
WHERE m.MATERIAL_ID IN ('RM-103','CMP-320','SEMI-060','FILL-2001','FILL-2002','SEMI-044','SEMI-045','FILL-1001','FILL-1002','FILL-1003','FG-2001','FG-2002','FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003')
SELECT * FROM dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL WHERE MATERIAL_ID IN ('CMP-320','SEMI-044','SEMI-045','SEMI-060')

SELECT i.DC_ID, i.MATERIAL_ID, i.SNAPSHOT_DT, i.ON_HAND_UNITS, i.SAFETY_STOCK_UNITS FROM dbo.DC_INV i WHERE i.MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003','FG-2001','FG-2002') AND i.SNAPSHOT_DT=(SELECT MAX(SNAPSHOT_DT) FROM dbo.DC_INV) ORDER BY 2,1

SELECT DC_ID, MATERIAL_ID, COUNT(*) n, SUM(UNITS) units_13wk, MIN(SHIP_DT) mn, MAX(SHIP_DT) mx FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP WHERE MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003','FG-2001','FG-2002') AND SHIP_DT > DATEADD(week,-13,'2026-09-30') GROUP BY DC_ID, MATERIAL_ID ORDER BY 2,1
SELECT DC_ID, MATERIAL_ID, SNAPSHOT_DT, ON_HAND_UNITS, SAFETY_STOCK_UNITS FROM dbo.DC_INV WHERE MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002') AND SNAPSHOT_DT >= '2026-07-01' ORDER BY 2,1,3
SELECT PLANT_ID, LEFT(MATERIAL_ID, CHARINDEX('-',MATERIAL_ID)) pfx, COUNT(*) n FROM dbo.PLANT_MATERIAL GROUP BY PLANT_ID, LEFT(MATERIAL_ID, CHARINDEX('-',MATERIAL_ID)) ORDER BY 1,2
SELECT SUPPLIER_ID, MATERIAL_ID, STATUS, COUNT(*) n, SUM(QTY) qty, MAX(PROMISED_SHIP_DT) mx FROM dbo.PURCH_ORD WHERE MATERIAL_ID IN ('CMP-320') GROUP BY SUPPLIER_ID, MATERIAL_ID, STATUS

SELECT s.WHSLR_ID, s.MATERIAL_ID, DATEPART(month,SHIP_DT) mo, SUM(UNITS) u, COUNT(*) n FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP s WHERE DC_ID='DC-EAST' AND MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002') AND SHIP_DT>='2026-06-01' GROUP BY s.WHSLR_ID, s.MATERIAL_ID, DATEPART(month,SHIP_DT) ORDER BY 2,1,3
SELECT DC_ID, WHSLR_ID, COUNT(*) n, SUM(UNITS) u FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP GROUP BY DC_ID, WHSLR_ID ORDER BY 1,2

S-111 (Kingsley Excipients) is qualified in SUPPLIER_MATERIAL and APPROVED/ACTIVE in the supplier portal for PL-01. RM-103 feeds SEMI-044/SEMI-045 -> Lacrivia 5/10 mL (FG-1001/1002) and Cyclosporine 0.05% (FG-1003). Need-by reflects S-111 standard ~23-day lead time; please expedite earlier if possible. Incremental to open S-111 PO000228 (5,300, promised 2026-10-17).

escalation_cases.subject: S-103 RM-103 (Glycerin USP) next shipment 4 weeks late – PO update, PL-02 coverage gap, follow-on PO risk
escalation_cases.details:
S-103 (Castellan Excipients) will miss its next RM-103 shipment by ~4 weeks: PO000210 (3,300 units, promised ship 2026-10-03 -> ~2026-10-31). Mitigation done: PR-BA7384C1 raised to alternate S-111 (Kingsley Excipients) for 3,300 units ship-to PL-01, need-by 2026-10-23 (please convert to PO and expedite).
Actions needed from Procurement/Supplier Quality (outside my tools):
1) Update PO000210 promised date in ERP to S-103's confirmed revised date, and confirm in writing whether S-103's following open RM-103 POs are also affected: PO000211 (4,400, 10-10), PO000212 (2,200, 10-18), PO000213 (5,900, 10-25).
2) PL-02 gap: S-103 is portal-approved for RM-103 at PL-01 and PL-02, but S-111 is approved for PL-01 ONLY. I did NOT order S-111 material to PL-02. RM-103 is in the PL-02 chain via CMP-320 (buffer/preservative concentrate, 0.3/unit) -> SEMI-060 latanoprost bulk -> Oculon 2.5 mL / 5 mL (FG-2001/FG-2002, NDC 99101-0303-25/-50). CMP-320 is bought from S-202 (primary) / S-203; please confirm (a) what RM-103 S-103 ships to PL-02 for, and (b) whether S-202/S-203 rely on S-103 glycerin. If PL-02 is exposed, start an expedited site approval of S-111 for PL-02 or confirm PL-02 RM-103 stock covers ~4 weeks.
3) Plant-level RM-103 on-hand is not available in the supply warehouse, so I could not compute plant days-of-cover. Please have PL-01/PL-02 confirm coverage through 2026-10-31.

escalation_cases.subject: DC-EAST Lacrivia (FG-1001/FG-1002) below safety stock – at risk from RM-103 delay; stock transfer decision needed
escalation_cases.details:
Context: S-103 RM-103 (Glycerin USP) next shipment ~4 weeks late (PO000210 -> ~2026-10-31). RM-103 feeds PL-01 Lacrivia/cyclosporine bulk. Alternate supply raised: PR-BA7384C1 (S-111, 3,300 to PL-01, need-by 2026-10-23). Supplier follow-up: CASE-518E77A4.
Finding (DC_INV snapshot 2026-09-25; WHSLR_SHIP last 13 weeks):
- FG-1001 Lacrivia 5 mL (NDC 99101010105): DC-EAST on hand 46 vs safety stock 471, ~237 units/wk demand (<1 wk cover). DC-CENTRAL 677 (SS 314, ~158/wk), DC-WEST 593 (SS 261, ~124/wk).
- FG-1002 Lacrivia 10 mL (NDC 99101010110): DC-EAST 34 vs SS 233, ~110/wk. DC-CENTRAL 351 (SS 155, ~74/wk), DC-WEST 324 (SS 129, ~65/wk).
- DC-EAST has been falling since 2026-08-21 while shipments to W-01/W-02 stayed steady, so this looks like a replenishment problem, not a demand spike. It started before the RM-103 slip, but a PL-01 slowdown would make it worse.
- FG-1003 and Oculon FG-2001/2002 are above safety stock at all DCs.
Suggested option for your decision: rebalance from DC-CENTRAL/DC-WEST to DC-EAST. FG-1001 stock above safety stock is 363 (CENTRAL) + 332 (WEST). FG-1002 is 196 + 195. Splitting weeks of cover evenly across the three DCs means moving about 276 (CENTRAL) + 278 (WEST) units of FG-1001 and about 120 + 135 of FG-1002, which would take the donor DCs below safety stock. If DC-EAST still falls short, you could then approve an allocation plan for W-01 (Keystone) and W-02 (Atlas) based on their shipment history.
Why I did not file the transfer/allocation approval: the approval form needs a USD value and neither warehouse has unit cost or price data. The wholesaler inventory feed also returned 503 (not ingested), so I could not check how much stock is in the channel. Please supply the valuation or file the transfer. I did not create any allocation or customer notice.
